title: Existence of balanced integral reindexing maps
statement: Fix the data of [def-sf-adic-realization-isomorphism-data] and a function-normalized RingReindex B as in [def-sf-native-adic-reindexing-data]. For every finite coefficient field E there is an IntegralReindex map I(E) for B.

source.place: BS Remark 6.8.15; HRS Lemma 7.9; explicit subargument of lem-sf-adic-reindexing-core, not a verbatim statement of either source.

proof.text: Compare the maps from pulled-back finite constant coefficient sheaves to finite continuous coefficient sheaves by the uniqueness of constant-section-normalized transport. Cancel the finite presentation isomorphism and evaluate on each point, using finite_constants on both schemes. Compose the two completed maps with each finite quotient projection, apply the preceding finite square, and use integral_residues. Joint monicity of the inverse-limit projections gives naturality of the integral presentation.

Precompose the proposed coefficient square with the invertible integral presentation. Cancel that presentation in the structural coefficient maps. Function normalization of RingReindex and the integral and rational inclusion normalizations identify the resulting maps pointwise. Invert the coefficient transport maps to obtain the restriction-of-scalars square; its components are identity linear equivalences on sections, with linearity given by that square.

Take the mate of this restriction square under the normalized scalar-extension adjunctions. The module transports are equivalences, so the mate is an isomorphism. Evaluate its unit equation at a local section to get the pure-section rule at scalar one; scalar linearity and inverse transport of the scalar give the rule for every scalar. Invert this mate to obtain balance and its specified sections equation.

Transfer the universal homotopy-category scalar-extension counits to cochain complexes. Apply the left-derived exact-equivalence square to balance and the two exact module transports. Its universal factorization equation is precisely integralReindexRepresentative after unfolding the cochain counits. Combine balance, sections, the derived comparison and this equation into IntegralReindex, and choose one such structure independently for every coefficient field.

proof_origin.place: BS Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; finite residue normalization, scalar-adjunction mate and universal derived-counit comparison.

theorem exists_integral_reindexing_maps (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (d : ∀ T : GeometricSpace D, SpaceData l D T)
    (T U : GeometricSpace D) (g : T.base.left ≅ U.base.left)
    (B : RingReindex l T.base.left g.hom (d T).realization (d U).realization) :
    letI := (d T).units
    letI := (d U).units
    Nonempty (∀ E, IntegralReindex l T.base.left g.hom B E)
